escalations.question: ErrorCategory member set: keep five matching backend-conventions.md section 2 (adding Forbidden), or reduce to the two members actually produced (Validation, NotFound)?

options.summary: Five members matching the conventions, plus a real consumer via ResultMessage
options.rationale: backend-conventions.md section 2 names the set explicitly; CORE-007 closes with 'align the member set with the conventions either way'. The half that bites -- no production caller reads the category -- is closed by ResultMessage regardless.

options.summary: Reduce to Validation and NotFound, grow it again when a caller needs the distinction
options.rationale: CORE-007's own first-listed alternative. Closes the 'never produced' observation literally, at the cost of deviating from a rung-1 authority's named set.

escalations.answer: Keep five members matching backend-conventions.md section 2, adding Forbidden, with ResultMessage as the production consumer. This is what the architect drafted; no amendment needed.

escalations.question: Does the Gate 1 'full redesign' of MASTER-088 require a genuinely non-generic Result type, or is Result<Unit> sufficient?

options.summary: Result<Unit> -- one dispatch path, one behavior arity, one handler interface
options.rationale: CORE-006 offers both readings explicitly: 'a non-generic Result (or a Unit payload)'. Both halves of the Gate 1 decision are satisfied either way, and this is materially the smaller T2 and T6.

options.summary: A genuinely non-generic Result alongside Result<T>
options.rationale: dotnet-format.md section 3's static-factory fragments show a bare Result. Requires a parallel ICommand, ICommandHandler<TCommand> and IPipelineBehavior<TCommand> plus a third dispatcher branch -- a materially larger T2 and T6.

escalations.answer: Adopt a genuinely non-generic Result alongside Result<T>, reversing the architect's draft. The user declined to decide on preference and asked for the more commonly accepted practice. The two-lookup budget was spent and did NOT return a citable answer to this specific question, so the decision rests on judgment and is recorded as belief, not standard: FluentResults and CSharpFunctionalExtensions both ship a non-generic Result alongside Result<T>; ErrorOr uses a placeholder (ErrorOr<Success>), which is the Unit shape; and MediatR -- the closest analogue to this repo's hand-rolled dispatcher -- removed Unit in v12 in favour of a non-generic request path. Three of four favour non-generic and the CQRS-specific precedent migrated off Unit. The user accepted the resulting increase in T2 and T6 effort in advance.
